text: Fiona, the hippo famous for surviving, is on 24-hour medical watch after eating a hat. World·New # Fiona, the hippo famous for surviving, is on 24-hour medical watch after eating a hat ## Hippo at Cincinnati Zoo is being treated for dehydration, nausea and pain A beloved hippopotamus named Fiona is on 24-hour medical watch after eating a knit hat that was tossed into her enclosure. Now the nine-year-old hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo, who became a social media darling after she was born prematurely and survived against all odds, is being treated for dehydration, nausea and pain, a staff member said in a social media update posted Tuesday. The incident happened about 10 days ago. At first, Fiona was asymptomatic, the staff member said, adding that "she's large enough that a small hat should be passing through." But after a few days her appetite decreased. Staff sedated her, ran an ultrasound and gave her rectal fluids but she still hasn't passed the hat. Now, they've giving her anti-nauseants, painkillers and medications to encourage her to eat. "Surgery isn't an option for full-grown hippos," the staff member said. "The best bet for Fiona would be if she could pass this on her own." A social media update on Fiona the hippo posted by the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden on Nov. 17, 2026. (@CincinnatiZoo/Instagram) Staff sedated her for more diagnostics this week, gave her more fluids and enemas and used a 2.7-metre scope to give Fiona a colonoscopy — but couldn't reach the hat. An ultrasound showed some bunching in her intestines, the zoo added. "At this point, what we can do is supportive care," the staff member said. "We're trying to give her all her favourite foods in hope she'll keep passing things through." - Canadian who stole a Las Vegas flamingo after drinking '30 to 40' beers convicted of animal cruelty - Lions and tigers are kept legally in Ontario backyards. No one knows how many there are The cap got into Fiona's habitat after it was tossed into the air by a visitor and caught by a ceiling fan that catapulted it through a small opening above the area's viewing windows, zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley told The Canadian Press. In another social media post about the incident, zoo staff asked visitors to help keep animals safe by securing their belongings and taking extra care near habitats. "Ingesting foreign objects can cause serious health problems for animals. If something falls into a habitat, please notify a zoo staff member immediately," the zoo wrote. CBC News has reached out to the zoo for more information. Fiona eats her specialty birthday cake to celebrate turning three years old in her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden on Jan. 23, 2020. (John Minchillo/The Associated Press) ## Famous for surviving Fiona weighed just 13 kilograms when she was born six weeks prematurely in 2017, the zoo previously posted. Most hippos are born weighing between 23 and 50 kilograms. "She is the smallest hippo to ever survive," the zoo said. Her fight to survive grabbed international attention. Fans followed her progress online and she became so popular that books were written about her. She also inspired a line of beer, all sorts of clothing and an ice cream flavor. Fiona sleeps in her enclosure on June 26, 2018. (John Minchillo/The Associated Press) Now, her fans around the world are following her care, many using the hashtag #teamfiona. Several other zoos and aquariums from Kansas to Honolulu commented on the Cincinnati Zoo's health update, urging Fiona to keep fighting and to pass the hat. "We are rooting for her and hoping that she proves to be as strong and resilient as she was at the beginning of her life," the zoo wrote online. "You got this Fiona!! Get that hat out girl!" a fan commented. "Please poop, Fiona," commented another person. With files from the Canadian Press
